llm.reply:
The genes linked to cystic fibrosis in the knowledge graph start with NCBIGene:1080 [1]. Its name is CF transmembrane conductance regulator [1]. Two further genes carry the association, NCBIGene:2212 [3] and NCBIGene:7040 [4].

## Associated gene records

The disease record in question is named Cystic fibrosis [2]. The gene NCBIGene:2212 is named Fc gamma receptor IIa [3]. The gene NCBIGene:7040 is named transforming growth factor beta 1 [4].

## Clinical features

The MedGen concept for the disease is titled Cystic fibrosis [6]. Its listed clinical features include Bronchiectasis [15]. They also include Clubbing of fingers [19]. Another listed feature is Hepatosplenomegaly [30].

## Literature context

Liver disease is common in cystic fibrosis, but encephalopathy is uncommon [26: "encephalopathy is a rare complication"]. Hyperammonemic encephalopathy can be triggered in previously stable liver disease, including by steroids [26: "can be precipitated in previously stable CFLD by various triggers including systemic corticosteroids"]. One indexed paper is titled Azithromycin and cystic fibrosis. [18].

## Trials

One registered trial is titled Assessment of Quadriceps Muscle Electrostimulation Used in Patients Suffering From Cystic Fibrosis [8]. Another is titled Pregnancies and Cystic Fibrosis [24].

The knowledge graph links three genes to cystic fibrosis. The first is NCBIGene:1080, CF transmembrane conductance regulator [1]. The second is NCBIGene:2212, Fc gamma receptor IIa [3]. The third is NCBIGene:7040, transforming growth factor beta 1 [4].

## Disease Record

The disease is recorded under the name Cystic fibrosis [2]. Its MedGen record is titled Cystic fibrosis [6]. PubTator3 indexes it as the literature entity Cystic Fibrosis [7].

## Clinical Features

The MedGen record lists Asthma as a clinical feature [11]. It lists Bronchiectasis [15]. It lists Clubbing of fingers [19]. It lists Dehydration [23]. It lists Diarrhea [27]. It lists Hemoptysis [28]. It lists Hepatomegaly [29]. It lists Hepatosplenomegaly [30].

## Literature

One indexed paper is Encephalopathy in cystic fibrosis. [5]. It reports that liver disease is common in cystic fibrosis and encephalopathy is rare [26: "encephalopathy is a rare complication"]. Other titles are 3.22 Nutrition in Cystic Fibrosis. [10]. Another is Editorial: Cystic Fibrosis in Children. [14]. Another is Azithromycin and cystic fibrosis. [18]. Another is Editorial: Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes. [22]. The linked publications include 32800451 [9]. They include 35240644 [13]. They include 35592838 [17]. They include 35853636 [21]. They include 39129918 [25].

## Clinical Trials

One trial is Assessment of Quadriceps Muscle Electrostimulation Used in Patients Suffering From Cystic Fibrosis [8]. Another is Pregnancies and Cystic Fibrosis [24]. The search also returned several trials on fibrocystic breast conditions rather than cystic fibrosis. One is A Study of Topical Danazol for the Treatment of Pain Associated With Fibrocystic Breast Disease [12]. Another is Efficacy and Safety of ONCOXIN in Patients With Breast Fibrocystic Disease [16]. Another is A Clinical Study on the Efficacy and Safety of the Treatment of Hyperplasia of Mammary Glands With Xiaoru Sanjie Capsule [20].
